JORES 09765006849 Dear Ms. Jores: This pertains to your letter dated April 21, 2025, in which you seek the Department's guidance regarding police assistance in the eviction of occupants from a privately- owned property. To be more precise, you wish to be clarified on whether DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2014-821 is applicable to your case. DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2014-82 pertains to the "Guidelines on Requesting Police Assistance in Demolition or Eviction Activities" issued pursuant to the Urban Development and Housing Act (UDHA). It governs requests for police assistance in demolitions involving underprivileged and homeless citizens, typically within the context of informal settlements and urban housing development programs. Said guidelines require, among others: A formal written request to the PNP Regional Director at least ten (IO) days before the scheduled demolition; Submission of certified true copies of the court order and notice of eviction by the Chairperson of the Local Housing Board; and The conduct of a pre-demolition conference by the Presidential Commission for the Urban Poor (PCUP), with notice to stakeholders such as the DSWD, CHR, DILG, LGU officials, representatives of the affected families, the landowner, and the issuing court. In contrast, the case you presented involves the execution of a court-issued writ of possession in a civil case involving a privately-owned property, which falls outside the ambit of DILG MC No. 2014-82. Instead, the applicable legal basis is Section IO(c), Rule 39 of the 2019 Amendments to the 1997 Rules of Civil Procedure, which provides: I Guidelines on Requesting for Police Assistance in Demolition or Eviction Activities under the Urban Development and Housing Act. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

Delivery or restitution of real property. — The officer shall demand of the person against whom the judgment for the delivery or restitution of real property is rendered and all persons claiming rights under him to peaceably vacate the property within three (3) working days, and restore possession thereof to the judgment obligee; otherwise, the officer shall oust all such persons therefrom with the assistance, if necessary, of appropriate peace officers, and employing such means as may be reasonably necessary to retake possession, and place the judgment obligee in possession of such property. As such, the court sheriff implementing the writ is authorized to request police assistance in executing the order. The law recognizes the sheriffs authority to call upon the PNP in cases of anticipated resistance or non-compliance, ensuring the peaceful and effective enforcement of court decisions. In view of the foregoing, the DILG MC No. 2014-82 does not apply to your case. Instead, the matter falls under the jurisdiction and enforcement authority of the courts and their implementing sheriffs, who may seek the assistance of the police as necessary in accordance with judicial rules and procedures. This opinion is rendered without prejudice to any contrary findings or interpretation by the courts or other competent authorities. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. ENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs page 2 of 2
